sentences.text: Both the petitioners and respondent no.2-complainant are present in the Court and have been duly identified by the IO and their respective counsels.

2. Pursuant to court notice issued by this Court vide previous order dated 11th April, 2023, the learned counsels who had appeared for the petitioners and respondent no.2-complainant during the mediation proceedings, are present.

This was done to ascertain veracity of the respondent no.2's submission that there was a verbal assurance given pursuant to the mediation regarding return of her certain articles, which she has not received.
3. A perusal of settlement agreement would show that it was recorded with the facilitation of Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts.

Moreover, as per para 3 of the said settlement, it has been recorded that the petitioner no.1-husband had agreed to pay a total sum of Rs.5.5 lacs to the respondent no.2-complainant by way of full and final settlement including istridhan, claim towards maintenance, permanent alimony and other receivables.
The said amount had been duly paid and received by respondent This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:55:00 no.2-complainant.
4. Thereafter, the parties have proceeded to cooperate to get divorce by mutual consent.

It was undertaken by respondent no.2-complainant in the settlement that she would cooperate in the quashing proceedings and in case of any default of any of the terms and conditions of the settlement,
the other party will be at liberty to initiate contempt proceedings.

sentences.text: These aspects have been pointed out to respondent no.2 who states that notwithstanding her claim that she has not received some of her articles from petitioner no.1, she is ready and willing to give her consent in order to achieve culmination of the matrimonial issues by quashing of the FIR.

6. Notwithstanding her consent, learned counsel for the petitioners states on instructions, that even if at this stage any of her articles are in their possession, the family of the petitioner will take steps to return the same to her in good faith.

7. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No. 385/2018 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Rajouri Garden and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
8. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
9. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
10. Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
11. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J MAY 18, 2023/sm
